Char: Study name: The establishment of clinical protocol for the induction of labour with double-balloon catheter and intravaginal misoprostol in gestational diabetes mellitus
Char: Participants:
600 women with gestational diabetes mellitus

Inclusion criteria: pregnant women with a single head position and a bishop cervical score less than 6, who meet the diagnostic criteria for gestational diabetes, have not experienced prelabour rupture of membranes (PROM), are at a gestational age of 40 weeks or more, have undergone regular birth examinations, delivered at a hospital, and have complete clinical data.

Exclusion criteria: women with fetal death, poor blood sugar control, or those who use insulin to control blood sugar during pregnancy; vaginal cleanliness rating of III or above, or visible fungal spores (GV) or trichomonas (Tri) detected in vaginal secretions before placing the balloon; positive (+) bacterial vaginosis sialidase (BV) test; high-risk complications during pregnancy, such as fetal distress, oligohydramnios, hypertensive disorder complicating pregnancy, etc.; placenta previa and vasa previa; severe comorbidities and complications, such as severe abnormal functions of heart, kidney and liver, which may prevent vaginal delivery; history of cesarean section or uterine surgery; obvious cephalopelvic disproportion; cervical cancer; certain infectious diseases of the genital tract, such as the active phase of herpes infection; untreated acquired immunodeficiency virus infection; people with heart disease, acute liver and kidney disease, severe anemia, glaucoma, asthma, epilepsy; people who are allergic to induced drugs; history of precipitous labor; and those who have had more than three deliveries.
Char: Interventions: Balloon catheters Vs Vaginal misoprostol
Char: Outcomes: Vaginal birth within 24 hours and fetal distress

Char: Study name: MEchanical DIlatation of the Cervix in a Scarred uterus (MEDICS)
Char: Participants:
100 women

Inclusion criteria: women ≥21 years of age (legal age of consent in Singapore) with one previous uncomplicated caesarean section who are potential trial of labor after cesarean candidates, with current singleton pregnancies of gestational age ≥37 weeks and with no contraindications to vaginal delivery.

Exclusion criteria: refusal to be randomised; opting for elective repeat caesarean section; ≥2 previous caesarean section; a previous classical or lower segment vertical incision; inverted T or J incision in the previous caesarean section; any structural abnormality of the uterus; multifetal pregnancy; placenta praevia or accreta; clinical suspicion of chorioamnionitis at presentation; and other fetal contraindications to vaginal delivery
Char: Interventions: Balloon catheters Vs Vaginal dinoprostone (tablet or gel)
Char: Outcomes: Increase in Bishops score, active labour within 24 and 48 hours, time from induction to delivery, number of interventions required in total, mode of delivery, uterine hyperstimulation, placental abruption, cord prolapse, postpartum haemorrhage, third-degree/fourth- degree perineal tears, uterine rupture, conversion to malpresentation, fetal distress, meconium-stained liquor, neonatal Apgar score of <7 at 5 min, cord blood pH of ≤7.0, admission to neonatal intensive care unit, neonatal hypoxic-ischaemic encephalopathy, neonatal deathand infectious complications

Char: Study name: Efficacy and safety comparison of oral misoprostol versus vaginal misoprostol for induction of labour
Char: Participants:
130 women

Inclusion criteria: women with a live singleton pregnancy of > 37 weeks for obstetric or medical indication for induction, vertex presentation, prolonged pregnancy, Bishop score less than 5, and intact membrane without previous stripping.

Exclusion criteria: suspected cephalo-pelvic disproportion, previous caesarean section or history of uterine surgery, multiple gestations, malpresentation, any contraindication for vaginal delivery or prostaglandin administration and suspected chorioamnionitis, suspected fetal jeopardy, placenta previa, and grand multigravida.
Char: Interventions: Oral misoprostol (25 or 50 µg Vs Vaginal misoprostol
Char: Outcomes: Vaginal delivery within 24 hours, caesarean section, uterine tachysystole, and neonatal outcome.

Char: Study name: Comparison of mechanical dilatation versus medical method for induction of labour
Char: Participants:
100 women

Inclusion criteria: women with singleton pregnancy, gestation age > 28 weeks, cephalic presentation, poor Bishop score.

Exclusion criteria: evidence of spontaneous labour, know contraindications for induction of labour, known contraindications for misoprostol, significant vaginal bleeding, and previous scar on uterus.
Char: Interventions: Balloon catheters Vs  Vaginal misoprostol
Char: Outcomes: Time from induction to delivery

Char: Study name: Comparing drug versus drug with catheter in low risk first time pregnant mothers for labor induction
Char: Participants:
608 women

Inclusion criteria: women with singleton, cephalic presentation, live fetus, primigravida, gestational age > 37 to 40+6 weeks, low-risk pregnancy, intact membranes, and Bishops Score < 6.

Exclusion criteria: maternal fever, non-reassuring cardiotocography, previously unsuccessful induction of labour, allergy to Misoprostol or latex, and previous caesarean section.
Char: Interventions: Vaginal misoprostol Vs Balloon catheters plus misoprostol
Char: Outcomes: Time from induction to delivery, vaginal delivery, caesarean section, meconium stained liquor, uterine tachysystole with changes in the baby's heartbeats, endomyometritis, need for Terbutaline, chorioamnionitis, Apgar score < 7 at 5 minutes, haemorrhage, and neonatal intensive care unit admission.

Char: Study name: Comparing the use of oral misoprostol with vaginal misoprostol to facilitate spontaneous labour
Char: Participants:
588 women

Inclusion criteria: women with singleton pregnancy between 39-40 weeks, cephalic presentation with live fetus, bishop score < 6 at 39 weeks, lack of current indication for induction of labour, and gestational diabetes on medical nutrition therapy.

Exclusion criteria: ruptured membranes, unexplained vaginal bleeding, prior uterine incision, gestational hypertension, gestational diabetes on oral hypoglycaemic agents & insulin, estimated fetal weight >= 4000gm, bad obstetric history, pregnancy by assisted reproductive technology,
malpresentations, multiple gestation, uterine anomaly, and Bishop score >= 6.
Char: Interventions: Oral misoprostol (25 or 50 µg) Vs Vaginal misoprostol
Char: Outcomes: Gestational age at delivery, meconium aspiration, neonatal intensive care unit admission, mode of delivery, and Apgar score < 7 at 5 minutes.

Char: Study name: Role of tablet misoprostol in inducing labour in pregnant female and which route is more effective whether sublingual or pervaginal in terms of time interval
Char: Participants:
100 women

Inclusion criteria: women with singleton pregnancy, gestational age between 37 and 41 weeks or more, and necessitating induction due to medical or obstetrical reasons.

Exclusion criteria: rupture of membranes, multiple gestation, previous caesarean delivery, contraindications to the use of specific drugs, grand multiparity, uterine anomalies, placenta previa, cephalopelvic disproportion, non-reassuring fetal heart rate, and women in active labor upon admission.
Char: Interventions: Sublingucal or buccal misoprostol Vs Vaginal misoprostol
Char: Outcomes: Vaginal delivery within 24 hours, time from induction to delivery, doses of misoprostol used, failure of induction, caesarean section, uterine hyperstimulation, oxytocin augmentation, mode of delivery, and adverse neonatal outcomes.

Char: Study name: Safety and efficacy of oral v/s vaginally administered misoprostol for induction of labour in term pregnancies- a randomised controlled trial
Char: Participants:
154 women

Inclusion criteria: nulliparous and multiparous women at term (37-42 completed weeks of gestation) with first-trimester ultrasound-confirmed dates, carrying a singleton fetus in cephalic presentation, and demonstrating clinically adequate pelvis, reassuring fetal heart tracing, and a modified Bishop's score of less than 6. Additionally, inclusion encompasses cases of gestational diabetes mellitus, gestational hypertension, past-date pregnancies, oligohydramnios, and premature rupture of membranes (<6 hours). 

Exclusion criteria: women with severe systemic illnesses such as uncontrolled diabetes mellitus, severe pre-eclampsia, cardiac, renal, or hepatic disease, as well as cases of intrauterine growth restriction (IUGR), intrauterine deaths, and hypersensitivity to misoprostol or any prostaglandin analogue. Additionally, exclusion extends to patients with contraindications to induction and vaginal delivery, including cephalopelvic disproportion, malpresentation, fetal compromise, non-reassuring fetal heart rate pattern, previous scar, and antepartum haemorrhage. Patients who are unwilling to participate in the study are also excluded.
Char: Interventions: Oral misoprostol (25 or 50 µg) Vs Vaginal misoprostol
Char: Outcomes: Fetal distress and time from induction to delivery

Char: Study name: A study to compare artificial initiation of the labour process with a rubber catheter on an out-patient basis with the standard process of initiation of labour with vaginal tablets after admission in the hospital
Char: Participants:
200 women

Inclusion criteria: low-risk primiparous and multiparous women undergoing induction of labour due to being past their due dates.

Exclusion criteria: women with a history of previous lower segment cesarean section (LSCS), hypertension, or pre-eclampsia, as well as cases of intrauterine growth restriction (IUGR), oligohydramnios, diabetes, and low-lying placenta. Additionally, exclusion criteria include chorioamnionitis or rupture of membranes, a Bishop score exceeding 7, and a history of primary or secondary infertility. Patients exhibiting non-reactive non-stress tests (NST) are also excluded.
Char: Interventions: Balloon catheters Vs Vaginal misoprostol
Char: Outcomes: Time from induction to delivery,  endometritis, neonatal sepsis, mode of delivery, hyperstimulation, neonatal intensive care unit admission, APGAR scores, meconium-stained liquor, postpartum hemorrhage, cord pH (targeting a pH of 7), fetal loss, and patient satisfaction, total admission duration, vaginal delivery within 12 hours post-admission, and the duration of inpatient hospital stay before delivery.

Char: Study name: A comparative study of Dilapan-S and Foley balloon in softening of neck of womb before labour induction
Char: Participants:
300 women

Inclusion criteria: term pregnancies complicated by gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM), pregnancy-induced hypertension (PIH), or fetal growth restriction (FGR), which are planned for labour induction with the fetus presenting in cephalic position.

Exclusion criteria: multiple pregnancies, previous cesarean section, breech presentation, and any contraindication for vaginal delivery.
Char: Interventions: Osmotic cervical dilators Vs Balloon catheters
Char: Outcomes: Bishop score

Char: Study name: To evaluate between early and late induction of labor in term Prelabor rupture of membranes
Char: Participants:
100 women

Inclusion criteria: women with singleton fetus with cephalic presentation, gestational ages between 37 and 40 weeks, and confirmed spontaneous rupture of membranes through history and examination. Additionally, inclusion extends to primigravida or multigravida patients with absent or mild uterine contractions (1-2 contractions lasting for 10-15 seconds), viable fetuses, and a modified Bishop's score of less than 6. Participants are required to present to the labour room within 12 hours of prelabor rupture of membranes.

Exclusion criteria: multiple gestation, fetal malpresentation, cephalopelvic disproportion, previous cesarean section or major uterine surgery, as well as medical and obstetric complications such as preeclampsia, diabetes, heart disease complicating pregnancy, and placenta previa. Additionally, patients in active labor, those with oligohydramnios not due to prelabor rupture of membranes, evidence of fetal distress, meconium-stained liquor, chorioamnionitis, cord prolapse, or preterm prelabor rupture of membranes are excluded.
Char: Interventions: Vaginal dinoprostone (tablet or gel) Vs Expectant management

Char: Study name: A clinical trail to study the efficacy and safety of two types of dinoprostone medication ( single application of slow release vaginal insert VS multiple dose gel) for labor initiation
Char: Participants:
600 women

Inclusion criteria: singleton pregnancies at term (37 weeks or more gestation) with cephalic presentation and a Bishop score of 6 or less, regardless of whether membranes are intact or ruptured.

Exclusion criteria: women with a history of a scarred uterus (previous cesarean section, extensive myomectomy involving the uterine cavity, previous uterine rupture or dehiscence), para 4 or more, multiple pregnancies, estimated fetal weight exceeding 4 kilograms, abnormal cardiotocogram (CTG), or any contraindication for vaginal delivery (placenta previa, malpresentation, active genital herpes infection). Additionally, women with contraindications or hypersensitivity to dinoprostone are also excluded.
Char: Interventions: Vaginal dinoprostone (tablet or gel) Vs Controlled-relase dinoprostone vaginal pessary
Char: Outcomes: Time from induction to vaginal delivery, oxytocin augmentation, uterine hyperstimulation with changes in the baby's heartbeats, mode of delivery, APGAR score, neonatal intensive care unit admission, maternal morbidity, and patient satisfaction.

Char: Study name: Success rate of initiation of birth process at term by inserting a balloon into the cervix compared by inserting a vaginal delivery system (dinoprostone)
Char: Participants:
Inclusion criteria: women over 18 years with signed informed consent, singleton pregnancy with cephalic presentation, no preterm rupture of membranes, gestational age between 37+0 and 42+0 weeks, an unfavourable cervix (Bishop-Score of 6 or less), absence of contra-indications for pharmaceutical induction of labour, and no clinical signs of infection or inflammation (temperature below 37.5 degrees Celsius, white blood cell count below 20,000, C-reactive protein below 20).

Exclusion criteria: fetal malformation, presence of contra-indications for pharmaceutical induction of labour, placentation disorders, history of uterine surgery with opening of the uterine cavity including cesarean section, preterm rupture of membranes, multiple gestations, gestational age below 37+0 weeks, and a history of surgery for cervical tear.
Char: Interventions: Balloon catheters Vs Vaginal dinoprostone (tablet or gel)
Char: Outcomes: Time from induction to delivery, time from induction to cervical dilating progress, vaginal delivery, caesarean section, patient satisfaction, neonatal morbidity and mortality, APGAR score, birth weight, neonatal intensive care unit admission, maternal infection, and epidural anaesthesia.
Char: Contact information: Obstetrics & Gynecology Department, Medical University of Graz, email: obgyn@medunigraz.at
Char: Notes: Recruitment status: Authorised-recruitment may be ongoing or finished

Char: Study name: Clinical trial comparing a pharmacological method for inducing labor with the combination of a pharmacological and a mechanical method
Char: Participants:
Inclusion criteria: pregnant women with a term singleton pregnancy, cephalic presentation, reassuring fetal heart rate pattern, intact membranes, and an unfavorable cervix (Bishop score less than 6), who are admitted to our institution for labour induction.

Pre-randomization exclusion criteria: women refusal to participate, contraindications to misoprostol use as per the leaflet, severe preeclampsia, prematurity (<37 weeks gestation), previous cesarean section or uterine surgery, intrauterine growth restriction, situations increasing the risk of infections and chorioamnionitis, premature rupture of membranes, maternal colonization with Streptococcus agalactiae, multifetal gestation, breech presentation, and stillbirth. 

Post-randomization exclusion criteria: women withdrawal from the study during induction and adverse effects from the supracervical balloon, such as pain or maternal discomfort.
Char: Interventions: Vaginal misoprostol Vs Balloon catheters plus misoprostol
Char: Outcomes: Time from induction to delivery, requirement and dosage of drugs for cervical ripening and labour induction, requirement of analgesia in labour, adverse effects, mode of delivery, Bishop score at 12 and 24 hours, oxytocin augmentation, vaginal delivery within 12 and 24 hours, neonatal intensive care unit admission, APGAR score at 5 minutes, and umbilical artery pH.
Char: Notes: Recruitment status: Authorised-recruitment may be ongoing or finished

Char: Study name: Comparison of patient satisfaction between two methods of induction of labour: use of a balloon catheter on an outpatient basis compared to an inpatient treatment with the medication "Propess"
Char: Participants:
138 women

Inclusion criteria: women aged over 18 years with a single pregnancy, fetal skull position, gestational age between 37+0 to 42+0 weeks, timely fetal development, Bishop score of less than 6, intact amniotic sac, no history of previous uterine surgeries, absence of contraindications for labour induction, and no signs of amnion infection syndrome.

Exclusion criteria: known intolerance to the investigational products or similar chemical structures, preterm rupture of membranes, known placentation disorder, previous caesarean section or cervix rupture, vaginal bleeding, fetal abnormalities, maternal disorders posing an elevated risk for fetal distress or maternal complications, and intrauterine death.
Char: Interventions: Balloon catheters Vs Controlled-release dinoprostone vaginal pessary
Char: Outcomes: Number of labour induction attempts until the development of contractions, caesarean section, neonatal outcome, epidural anaesthesias, and women satisfaction.
Char: Contact information: Clinical Trials Information, Medizinische Universität Graz, email: ev.weiss@medunigraz.at
Char: Notes: Recruitment status: Authorised-recruitment may be ongoing or finished

Char: Study name: The Home Induction trial: A randomised open-label trial to assess outpatient induction of labour, and compare efficacy of Propess vs Dilapan-S® for induction of labour at 39 weeks’ gestation in normal risk nulliparous women
Char: Participants:
327 women

Inclusion criteria: normal-risk nulliparous women aged 18 to under 40 years with singleton pregnancies and no contraindications to labour induction. Participants must agree to outpatient induction at 39 weeks and have no relevant medical issues assessed by a doctor on a case-by-case basis, inclusive of systems disorders outlined in the exclusion criteria. They must live within 30 minutes or 15 km of the hospital and have transport available at all times during the induction period. Additionally, a normal amniotic fluid index (AFI) between 8 cm and 20 cm and a Biophysical Profile Score (BPS) of 8/8 at 39 weeks gestation is required. Furthermore, participants must have a Bishop's score of less than 6 at Visit 2.

Exclusion criteria: multiparous women with a uterine scar, low-lying placenta, BMI exceeding 35kg/m2, multiple gestation, known fetal anomalies, fetal growth restriction, or oligohydramnios, and maternal health problems such as hypertensive, cardiac, renal, diabetes, pulmonary, or hepatic diseases directly affecting the woman's risk status. Additionally, exclusion criteria include lack of transport to the hospital, living more than 30 minutes or 15 km away, difficulty understanding the protocol and follow-up instructions, and gestational age less than 39+0 or greater than 39+4 weeks at the time of induction. Other contraindications involve factors such as ongoing labour, previous uterine surgery, clinical suspicion of cephalopelvic disproportion, fetal malpresentation, non-reassuring fetal testing, history of major surgery or cervical rupture, pelvic inflammatory disease, hypersensitivity to dinoprostone, placenta previa, unexplained vaginal bleeding, or evidence of infection.
Char: Interventions: Controlled-release dinoprostone vaginal pessary Vs Osmotic cervical dilators
Char: Outcomes: Failure to achieve vaginal delivery, change in Bishop score before and after cervical ripening, vaginal delivery at 36 and 48 hours, the need for second induction modality, uterine hyperstimulation, length of hospital stay, adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes, maternal satisfaction, caesarean section, and use of analgesia.

Char: Study name: Labour induction in an outpatient setting - a multicenter randomized controlled trial. OPTION - OutPatienT InductiON
Char: Participants:
17,782 women

Inclusion criteria: women aged 18 to 45 years, capable of communicating with the hospital, and experiencing uncomplicated live singleton pregnancies at gestational ages between 37+0 to 41+6 weeks according to crown-rump length or biparietal diameter (<55 mm) on first or second-trimester ultrasound. Additionally, participants must have an engaged and stable cephalic presentation. Clinical examination before induction, including Leopold's maneuvers, digital cervical exam, abdominal ultrasound, temperature, blood pressure, and cardiotocography scan, must reveal an engaged and stable cephalic presentation with a Bishop score of less than 6 (less than 5 in parous women) and a cardiotocography classified as normal according to the antepartal Swedish Society of Obstetrics and Gynecology criteria. Furthermore, during the first 45 minutes after induction, in cases of induction with the balloon method, cardiotocography must be classified as normal according to the same criteria.

Exclusion criteria: a history of previous uterine surgery with uterine scar (e.g. caesarean section or myomectomy), pregestational or medically treated gestational diabetes (insulin or metformin), dietary treated gestational diabetes with large for gestational age fetus, preeclampsia or unstable hypertensive disease, multiple pregnancies, intrauterine fetal death (IUFD) in current or previous pregnancies, known fetal malformations or conditions affecting newborn care, congenital uterine malformations, conditions requiring inpatient care, and inability to reach the hospital within a reasonable time. Clinical examination before induction must exclude small for gestational age (small for gestational age (SGA), intrauterine growth restriction (IUGR), or fetal growth restriction (FGA), oligohydramnios, polyhydramnios, maternal pyrexia, known low-lying placenta, and high head. Additionally, exclusion criteria include premature rupture of membranes (PROM) exceeding 30 hours or known colonization with group B streptococci. Observations within the first 45 minutes after induction must also consider adverse events such as heavy bleeding, pain, and premature rupture of membranes, if not the indication for induction, as well as the start of contractions.
Char: Interventions: Balloon catheters Vs Oral misoprosrol
Char: Outcomes: Severe perinatal morbidity or mortality, vaginal delivery, mother admitted to intensive care unit, and post-partum bleeding >1000 ml.
Char: Contact information: OPTION study, Sahlgrenska University Hospital, Diagnosvägen 15 41650 Gothenburg Sweden, email: OPTION@vgregion.se
Char: Notes: Recruitment status: Authorised-recruitment may be ongoing or finished

Char: Study name: The comparison of drug and mechanical methods for cervical ripening before delivery
Char: Participants:
120 women

Inclusion criteria: women at gestational age over 37 weeks, singleton gestation, cephalic presentation, intact amniotic sac, absence of contraindications to misoprostol use, and being primigravida with a Bishop score of 3 to 4.

Exclusion criteria: allergy to misoprostol, elective cesarean section, urgent delivery by cesarean section, intrauterine growth restriction (IUGR), placenta previa, fetal bradycardia, placental abruption, massive bleeding, and a history of previous cesarean section.
Char: Interventions: Vaginal misoprostol Vs Balloon catheters
Char: Outcomes: Ripening of cervix, caesarean section, fetal bradycardia, meconium in amnionic fluid, uterine hyperstimulation, and uterine rupture.

Char: Study name: Comparison of the effect of misoprostol with oxytocin in companion with a cervical catheter in the induction of labor: a clinical trial
Char: Participants:
50 women

Inclusion criteria: women at gestational age 37 weeks and over with indications for termination, primiparous women, singleton pregnancies, reassuring fetal heart rate, cephalic presentation, intact fetal membranes, ineffective labour contractions, and a Bishop Score of 6 or below.

Exclusion criteria: misoprostol allergy, fever over 38 °C, history of uterine surgery and cesarean, obstetric indication for cesarean delivery, anaemia and blood dyscrasia, and asthma.
Char: Interventions: Balloon catheters plus oxytocin Vs Balloon catheters plus misoprostol
Char: Outcomes: Ripen of cervix, duration of latent phase of labour, active of labour, second stage of labour, and adverse outcomes.

Char: Study name: Comparison of Transcervical Catheter and Laminaria efficacy on induction of labor
Char: Participants:
100 women

Inclusion criteria: pregnant women with post-term pregnancy eligible for induction of labour, having a Bishop score of less than 5, and a fetus in vertex presentation.

Exclusion criteria: spontaneous contractions, rupture of membranes, and a uterine scar, Bishop score greater than 5, placenta previa, and any contraindication to vaginal delivery.
Char: Interventions: Balloon catheters Vs Osmotic cervical dilators
Char: Outcomes: Time from induction to delivery and time from induction to active phase of labour

Char: Study name: Effect of sublingual Misoprostol in inducing labor
Char: Participants:
70 women

Inclusion criteria: women with gestational ages between 37 and 42 weeks, Bishop Score of 4 or less, indication for labour induction, cephalic presentation, and reactive non-stress test (NST).

Exclusion criteria: Bishop score greater than 4, gestational ages less than 37 and more than 42 weeks, non-vertex presentation, intrauterine demise, previous uterine surgery, oligo or polyhydramnios, intrauterine growth retardation, multiple pregnancies, clinical evidence of cardiopulmonary collapse, electrolyte abnormalities, severe pre-eclampsia/eclampsia, hepatitis, asthma, glaucoma, and adrenal insufficiency.
Char: Interventions: Sublingual or buccal misoprostol Vs Oxytocin (alone)
Char: Outcomes: Vaginal delivery and caesarean section.

Char: Study name: Comparison of characteristics of women undergoing labor induction with oxytocin and oral misoprostol
Char: Participants:
65 women

Inclusion criteria: women with gestational ages between 39 and 42 weeks, estimated fetal weight of 4000 g, normal fetal heart rate, cephalic presentation, absence of uterine contractions, singleton pregnancy, and a Bishop score of 7 or less.

Exclusion criteria: previous uterine surgery including caesarean section, intrauterine fetal death or intrauterine growth restriction (IUGR), oligohydramnios, placenta previa, umbilical cord prolapse, symptoms of chorioamnionitis, symptoms of active herpes, kidney or liver disease, non-reactive Non-Stress Test (NST), contraindication for administration of prostaglandin, contraindication for induction of labour, and vaginal bleeding of unknown cause.
Char: Interventions: Oral misoprostol (25 or 50 µg) Vs Oxytocin (alone)
Char: Outcomes: Time from induction to delivery and time from induction to active phase of labour.

Char: Study name: Comparison between misoprostol and oxytocine in cervical ripening for labour induction: a randomized clinical trial
Char: Participants:
190 women

Inclusion criteria: women requiring a medical indication for the induction of delivery, single or twin pregnancies, gestational age more than 36 weeks, vertex presentation, and normal heart rate of the fetus.

Exclusion criteria: embryo-pelvic dystocia, estimated fetal weight over 4000 grams or evidence of cephalopelvic disproportion, abnormal vaginal bleeding or any placenta previa, multiparity over 4 pregnancies, fetal malformation, previous uterine scar, any situation not indicating vaginal delivery, contraindications to the use of misoprostol, and severe polyhydramnios.
Char: Interventions: Vaginal misoprostol Vs Oxytocin
Char: Outcomes: Bishop score and APGAR score
Char: Contact information: Razie Mohamadjafari, email: alinazeri_76@yahoo.com, mnamazi1979@yahoo.com, and mohamadjafari-r@ajums.ac.ir

Char: Study name: Comparison of the effect of misoprostol and oxytocin on the induction of labor
Char: Participants:
90 women

Inclusion criteria: pregnant women aged 20-35 with a pregnancy term exceeding 37 weeks, absence of contraindications for normal delivery, no drug sensitivity to misoprostol and oxytocin, and absence of chronic diseases.

Exclusion criteria: participant dissatisfaction with attending the study, tearing of membranes, and limitations in fetal growth.
Char: Interventions: No treatment Vs Misoprostol Vs Oxytocin
Char: Outcomes: Time from induction to latent phase of labour and time from induction to active phase of labour.

Char: Study name: Traction effect with folly catheter on cervices ripening compared to vaginal misoprostol
Char: Participants:
120 women

Inclusion criteria: women referred to the Besat Hospital indicating the induction of labour, with a gestational age equal to or greater than 37 weeks, satisfaction to participate in the research, intact chorionic membrane, vertex presentation, single pregnancy, and an inappropriate cervix with a Bishop score of 4 or less.

Exclusion criteria: fetal distress, severe pre-eclampsia, intrauterine growth restriction, contraindications for the use of prostaglandins, regular uterine contractions, early placental detachment, placenta previa, vaginal bleeding, and a history of previous cesarean section or uterine surgery.
Char: Interventions: Vaginal misoprostol Vs Balloon catheters
Char: Outcomes: Time from induction to delivery and Bishop score

Char: Study name: Comparison of vaginal Misoprostol versus Foley catheter for labor induction
Char: Participants:
60 women

Inclusion criteria: women with cephalic presentation, a healthy amnion, a Bishop score less than 6, an inappropriate cervix, inappropriate uterine contractions, and a normal fetal heart rate.

Exclusion criteria: pelvic dystocia, fetal weight exceeding 4 kg, incompatibility of fetal head with maternal pelvis, placenta previa, unexplained vaginal bleeding, parity exceeding five, fetal anomaly, previous uterine scar, and any situation that renders vaginal delivery impossible.
Char: Interventions: Vaginal misoprostol Vs Balloon catheters
Char: Outcomes: Time from induction to delivery, haemorrhage, and APGAR score.

Char: Study name: Comparing the Effect of Oral Misoprostol and Intravenous Oxytocin on Labor Induction
Char: Participants:
140 women

Inclusion criteria: women with gestational age exceeding 42 weeks, primiparous or multiparous women over 18 years old, singleton pregnancy, and cervical ripeness indicated by a Bishop score greater than six.

Exclusion criteria: multiple pregnancies, need for cesarean section, history of uterine scarring, placenta previa, excessive postpartum vaginal bleeding, presence of heart, liver or kidney diseases, previous sensitivity to Oxytocin, Misoprostol, or prostaglandin analogues, and severe congenital anomalies in the fetus.
Char: Interventions: Oral misoprostol (25 or 50 µg) Vs Oxytocin (alone)
Char: Outcomes: Vaginal delivery within 48 hours, mode of delivery, and APGAR score.

Char: Study name: Comparison of the effect of simultaneous administration of oxytocin with Foley catheter with co-administration of misoprostol and Foley catheter on cervical preparation and duration of labor
Char: Participants:
74 women

Inclusion criteria: women with a live fetus, singleton pregnancy, gestational age equal to or greater than 40 weeks, cephalic presentation, absence of fetal anomaly, fetal weight estimate less than 4500 grams, Bishop Score less than 4, maternal age greater than 18, absence of parity exceeding 5, and absence of medical illnesses such as diabetes and high blood pressure.

Exclusion criteria: placental abruption, chorioamnionitis, rupture of the membrane before the catheter is expelled, previous caesarean section, gestational diabetes, placenta previa, and any contraindication for vaginal delivery.
Char: Interventions: Balloon catheters plus oxytocin Vs Balloon catheters plus misoprostol
Char: Outcomes: Mode of delivery, tachysystole, haemorrhage, and time from induction to delivery.

Char: Study name: The effect of oral and sublingual and buccal Misoprostol on induction of preterm premature rupture of membrane
Char: Participants:
120 women

Inclusion criteria: women with a single pregnancy, preterm premature rupture of membranes, gestational age between 37 and 42 weeks, cephalic presentation of the fetus, informed consent from the individual to participate in the study, low-risk pregnancy without complications such as preeclampsia, gestational diabetes, or heart diseases, satisfactory fetal heart rate patterns, absence of contraindications to natural childbirth, and no history of uterine scar.

Exclusion criteria: chorioamnionitis, fetal macrosomia, and the use of other methods of initiating induction within the last 7 days.
Char: Interventions: Oral misoprostol (25 or 50 µg) Vs Sublingual or buccal misoprostol
Char: Outcomes: Time from induction to delivery, APGAR score, neonatal intensive care unit admission, dystocia, neonatal sepsis, postpartum haemorrhage, and caesarean section.

Char: Study name: The Effect of Vaginal Isosorbide Mononitrate Administration on Cervical Ripening before Induction of Labor
Char: Participants:
64 women

Inclusion criteria: primigravida women with a gestational age over 40 weeks, singleton pregnancy, and a fetus in cephalic presentation with a Bishop score less than 4.

Exclusion criteria: primigravida women with a previous scar on the uterus, polyhydramnios, blood pressure exceeding 160/110, proteinuria equal to or greater than 1, a history of intolerance to isosorbide mononitrate, and being a candidate for cesarean section.
Char: Interventions: Nitric oxide donors Vs Placebo
Char: Outcomes: Bishop score and maternal blood pressure.

Char: Study name: Balloon catheter versus misoprostol for the induction of labor following pre-labor rupture of membranes at term
Char: Participants:
650 women

Inclusion criteria: women aged 18 years and above, whether primiparous or multiparous, with singleton pregnancies at a gestational age of 37 weeks or more. Additionally, participants must have experienced spontaneous rupture of membranes without the onset of labour within 18-48 hours, possess an unfavourable cervix (Bishop's score < 6), and have a cephalic presentation of the fetus. Importantly, they should also exhibit no colonization of Group B Streptococcus on vaginal and rectal swabs.

Exclusion criteria: pre-term pre-labour rupture of membranes (gestational age <37 weeks), clinical signs of infection like vaginitis or chorioamnionitis, and active infection or carrier status for HIV, hepatitis B, or hepatitis C. Additionally, exclusion criteria encompass conditions such as type 1 diabetes, Group B Streptococcal colonization, acute maternal or fetal conditions necessitating immediate delivery, and intrauterine growth restriction. Other factors like macrosomia (estimated fetal weight ≥4.5 kg), non-cephalic fetal presentation, previous caesarean section or uterotomy, and inadequate understanding or language proficiency to comprehend study materials are also considered. Importantly, refusal of participation or signed consent refusal is also grounds for exclusion.
Char: Interventions: Oral misorprostol (25 or 50 µg) Vs Balloon catheters
Char: Outcomes: Mode of delivery, retention of placenta, haemorrhage, birth canal tears, maternal infection, APGAR score, need for intubation, neonatal intensive care unit admission, and birth experience.

Char: Study name: Comparing two methods of labour induction in term pregnant women who had one previous Caesarean delivery and history of vaginal birth(s)
Char: Participants:
60 women

Inclusion criteria: women requiring induction of labour, with a history of one previous scar and previous vaginal births, aged 18 years and above. Additionally, participants must have a gestational age of over 37 weeks at enrolment, an unfavourable cervix (Bishop Score <6), and a singleton pregnancy with cephalic presentation. Furthermore, pre-induction fetal cardiotocography (CTG) should show reassuring patterns, and participants should have intact membranes. Importantly, the absence of significant contractions, defined as <2 contractions in 10 minutes, is also considered.

Exclusion criteria: a preference for elective repeated caesarean section, latex or prostaglandin allergies, and an inability to provide consent. Additionally, individuals with known gross fetal anomalies, absolute contraindications to vaginal delivery, or estimated fetal weights outside the range of <2 kg or ≥ 4 kg are also excluded.
Char: Interventions: Balloon catheters Vs Controlled-release dinoprostone vaginal pessaru
Char: Outcomes: Caesarean section, use of additional method for cervical ripening, Bishop score, oxytocin augmentation, use of analgesia, estimated blood loss, maternal infection, uterine rupture or scar, uterine hyperstimulation, Terbutaline use, maternal satisfaction, pain, APGAR score, atrerial cord pH, birth weight, neonatal intensive care unit admission, and neonatal complications.

Char: Study name: Oral versus vaginal administration of misoprostol for induction of labor in women with pre labour rupture of membranes. Results of a randomized controlled trial
Char: Participants:
51 women

Inclusion criteria: no information

Exclusion criteria: no information
Char: Interventions: Oral misoprostol (25 or 50 µg) Vs Vaginal misoprostol
Char: Outcomes: Time from induction to delivery.

Char: Study name: Efficacy and Safety of Hourly Titrated Misoprostol Versus Vaginal Dinoprostone and Misoprostol for Cervical Ripening and Labor Induction: Randomized Clinical Trial
Char: Participants:
372 women

Inclusion criteria: women over 18 with a single pregnancy and cephalic presentation of the fetus. Additionally, participants should have intact membranes, an unfavourable cervix with a Bishop score of less than 6, and a non-reactive decelerative cardiotocography.

Exclusion criteria: a history of prior caesarean section or previous uterine surgery, along with allergies or intolerance to any study drugs. Additionally, individuals with stillbirth, uterine growth-restricted fetuses, or contraindications for vaginal delivery are excluded. Other criteria encompass factors such as an anterior placenta, multiparity, moderate to severe heart disease, hypertensive disorders of pregnancy, suspected chorioamnionitis, coagulation disorders, a history of epileptic seizures, and liver or kidney disease. Furthermore, cognitive impairment or inadequate proficiency in Spanish are also grounds for exclusion.
Char: Interventions: Oral misoprostol Vs Vaginal misoprostol Vs Controlled-release dinoprostone vaginal pessary
Char: Outcomes: Vaginal delivery within 24 hours, cervical status, percentage of caesarean sections, use of oxytocin, duration of latent and active phases and the pushing stage of labour, induction failure, uterine tachysystole, hypertonicity, hyperstimulation, or rupture, adverse events including maternal and/or foetal death, pain, women’s satisfaction with the induction process, maternal morbidity, and foetal morbidity

Char: Study name: Comparison of Misoprostol and Prostaglandin E2 (PGE2) Gel for Induction of Labour in Premature Rupture of Membranes at Term
Char: Participants:
932 women

Inclusion criteria: premature rupture of membranes occurring at 37 weeks or later gestation. Additionally, eligibility extends to cases involving a single live fetus presenting in a cephalic position.

Exclusion criteria: women who are already in active labour, those presenting with contraindications for the induction of labour, and individuals with a history of previous caesarean section or uterine surgery.
Char: Interventions: Vaginal misoprostol Vs Vaginal dinoprostone
Char: Outcomes: Caesarean section, time from induction to delivery, and maternal and neonatal morbidity.

Char: Study name: Cervical Ripening Before Induction of Labour at Term: a Randomised Comparison of Prostin vs Propess
Char: Participants:
446 women

Inclusion criteria: singleton pregnancy, cephalic presentation of the fetus, gestational age exceeding 37 weeks as confirmed by ultrasound examination, and a Bishop score of less than 7.

Exclusion criteria: a history of previous cesarean section, indicative of a scarred uterus, the presence of polyhydramnios, the occurrence of multiple pregnancies, and the identification of fetal malformations.
Char: Interventions: Controlled-release dinoprostone vaginal pessary Vs Vaginal dinoprostone
Char: Outcomes: Vaginal delivery within 12, 24, 36, and 48 hours, hyperkinesia with or without fetal heart rate monitoring abnormalities, uterine hyperstimulation with or without changes of baby's heartbeats, APGAR score < 7 at 5 and 10 minutes, arterial pH, postpartum haemorrhage, and cervical dilation > 3cm.

Char: Study name: A Comparison of Transcervical Foley Catheter and Prostaglandins for Induction of Labor at Term
Char: Participants:
154 women

Inclusion criteria: nulliparous women with a singleton pregnancy, gestational age of 37 weeks or more. Additionally, candidates must exhibit a Bishop score of 5 or less, possess an intact amniotic membrane, and show no signs of active labour. Furthermore, the presence of a live fetus in vertex presentation and the absence of prior uterine surgical procedures are prerequisites for inclusion in the study.

Exclusion criteria: major congenital anomaly
Char: Interventions: Balloon catheters Vs Controlled-release dinoprostone vaginal pessary
Char: Outcomes: Successful labour induction, change of Bishop score, caesarean section, vaginal delivery within 24 hours, time from induction to delivery, neonatal intensive care unit admission, and pain.

Char: Study name: Foley Catheter Versus Dinoprostone Vaginal Insert for Induction of Labor in Parous Women at Term: A Randomized Trial
Char: Participants:
154 women

Inclusion criteria: nulliparous women with a singleton pregnancy, gestational age of 37 weeks or more. Additionally, candidates must exhibit a Bishop score of 5 or less, possess an intact amniotic membrane, and show no signs of active labour. Furthermore, the presence of a live fetus in vertex presentation and the absence of prior uterine surgical procedures are prerequisites for inclusion in the study.

Exclusion criteria: major congenital anomaly
Char: Interventions: Balloon catheters Vs Controlled-release dinoprostone vaginal pessary
Char: Outcomes: Successful labour induction, change of Bishop score, caesarean section, vaginal delivery within 24 hours, time from induction to delivery, NICU admission, and pain.

Char: Study name: A Study Comparing Vaginal Misoprostol and Intravenous Oxytocin for Induction of Labor
Char: Participants:
130 women

Inclusion criteria: women who are aged 18 years or older, multiparous, and carrying a singleton gestation. Additionally, they should have surpassed 37 weeks of gestation and exhibit a cephalic presentation.

Exclusion criteria: any clinical contraindication to misoprostol usage, women below 18 years of age, and those with contraindications to vaginal birth. Moreover, non-reassuring fetal heart rate tracing, prior uterine surgery, active labour, maternal bleeding, and chorioamnionitis are factors that preclude participation.
Char: Interventions: Vaginal misoprostol Vs Oxytocin (alone)
Char: Outcomes: Time from induction to delivery, time from induction to vaginal delivery, APGAR score, birth weight, mode of delivery, maternal satisfaction, uterine hyperstimulation, and neonatal intensive care unit admission.

Char: Study name: Oral Misoprostol Versus Vaginal Dinoprostone For Induction Of Labour: A Randomized Controlled Clinical Trial
Char: Participants:
342 women

Inclusion criteria: primigravida women with gestational age > 37 weeks

Exclusion criteria: scarred uterus and macrosomia
Char: Interventions: Oral misoprostol Vs Vaginal dinoprostone
Char: Outcomes: Time from induction to delivery

Char: Study name: The Comparison of Oxytocin Induced Labor and Cook Balloon Induced Labor
Char: Participants:
300 women

Inclusion criteria: women with a gestational age of 37 weeks or more, carrying a single fetus, and without any serious complications.
Char: Interventions: Balloon catheters Vs Oxytocin (alone)
Char: Outcomes: Success rate of induced labor

Char: Study name: Combined Method for Induction of Labor
Char: Participants:
300 women

Inclusion criteria: women requiring induction of labour

Exclusion criteria: women who have had a previous cesarean section or other uterine scars, such as those from a myomectomy. Additionally, refusal to participate in the study is also considered an exclusion criterion.
Char: Interventions: Vaginal misoprostol Vs Balloon catheters Vs Balloon catheters plus misoprostol
Char: Outcomes: Time from induction to delivery

Char: Study name: Randomized Control Trial of Intracervical Balloon Placement vs Oxytocin in Women With Term PROM and Unripe Cervices
Char: Participants:
200 women

Inclusion criteria: nulliparous women aged 18-50 years with singleton gestation, vertex presentation of a live fetus, and rupture of membranes confirmed by sterile speculum examination after 37 weeks of gestation, provided their Bishop score is less than 6.

Exclusion criteria: multiparous women with a Bishop score greater than 6, those with multifetal gestation, and those with contraindications to labor such as placenta previa. Additionally, women with a maternal fever prior to randomization exceeding 100.4°F and those with known fetal anomalies are also excluded.
Char: Interventions: Balloon catheters Vs Oxytocin (alone)
Char: Outcomes: Time from induction to delivery, length of first stage of labour, caesarean section, chorioamnionitis, endometritis, postpartum haemorrhage, epidural use, APGAR score, and neonatal umbilical arterial and venous acid base status.

Char: Study name: Balloon Induction of Labor in PROM for TOLAC
Char: Participants:
200 women

Inclusion criteria: singleton pregnancy with a previous single cesarean section, at least 12 months elapsed since the last caesarean delivery, confirmed premature rupture of membranes (PROM) at ≥34 weeks' gestation, membranes ruptured ≤24 hours before study inclusion, vertex presentation well applied to the cervix, unripe cervix as indicated by a speculum examination (Bishop score ≤6), absence of significant and regular uterine contractions (<3/10Min), willingness to comply with the study protocol, and signed informed consent (including a trial of labor after cesarean consent form).

Exclusion criteria: contraindication for vaginal delivery (e.g., placenta previa, non-vertex presentation, previous cesarean delivery <12 months), regular uterine contractions (>3/10Min), ruptured membranes diagnosed over 24 hours prior to study inclusion, meconium-stained amniotic fluid, evidence of chorio-amnionitis (body temperature 37.6°C with uterine tenderness and maternal or fetal tachycardia or purulent discharge or WBC20.000), suspected placental abruption or significant haemorrhage, and non-reassuring fetal status requiring immediate intervention as determined by fetal heart rate monitoring and/or bio-physical profile.
Char: Interventions: Balloon catheters Vs Expectant management
Char: Outcomes: Vaginal birth after caesarean section, PROM to delivery interval, intrapartum and post-partum infection, and caesarean section.

Char: Study name: Nitric Oxide Donor Isosorbide Mono Nitrate for Cervical Ripening in Induction of Labor
Char: Participants:
140 women

Inclusion criteria: Bishop score ≤ 6, singleton pregnancy, gestational age of 39 weeks or more, cephalic presentation of the fetus, average fetal size, and absence of pelvic contraction.

Exclusion criteria: any contraindication to labour induction as outlined by the American College of Obstetrics and Gynecology. Additionally, exclusion criteria include previous classical or inverted T-shaped or unknown uterine incision, previous hysterotomy/myomectomy involving entry of the uterine cavity or extensive myometrial dissection, previous uterine rupture, placenta previa or vasa previa, abnormal fetal lie, active genital herpes infection, major cephalopelvic disproportion, grand multipara, malpresentation, overdistension of the uterus such as polyhydramnios or multiple pregnancy, invasive carcinoma of the cervix, pregnancy following repair for vesicovaginal fistula, prelabour rupture of membranes, previous lower segment cesarean section, umbilical cord prolapse, established fetal distress, and complications such as heart disease, liver disease, or anaemia complicating pregnancy.
Char: Interventions: Nitric oxide donors Vs Placebo
Char: Outcomes: Time from induction to delivey

Char: Study name: Vaginal Misoprostol With Intracervical Foley Catheter in Induction of Labor
Char: Participants:
120 women

Inclusion criteria: singleton pregnancy with a gestational age of 37 weeks or more, as calculated from reliable menstrual dates and/or late first trimester or early second-trimester ultrasound; modified Bishop Score of 5 or more; a valid indication for induction of labour; intact fetal membranes; normal fetal non-stress test; cervical dilation less than or equal to 2cm; and vertex presentation.

Exclusion criteria: any contraindication for vaginal delivery (e.g. placenta previa, accrete); any contraindication for induction of labour (e.g. fetal malpresentation, prior uterine surgery); active labour; antepartum haemorrhage; eclampsia; patients with hemolysis, elevated liver enzymes, and low platelets; suspected chorioamnionitis; intrauterine growth retardation; multiple gestations; non-reassuring fetal heart rate; continuous contractions more than 3 times in 10 minutes at the onset of induction of labour; intrauterine fetal demise; any contraindication for the use of misoprostol (e.g. bronchial asthma, drug allergy, history of glaucoma); any contraindication for the use of Foley catheter (already ripped cervix); rupture of membranes; and not consent.
Char: Interventions: Balloon catheters plus misoprostol Vs Vaginal misoprostol
Char: Outcomes: Time from induction to delivey, total misoprstol needed, mode of delivery, maternal pyrexia, hypersystole, tachysystole, APGAR score, birth weight, and neonatal intensive care unit admission.

Char: Study name: Comparison of Two Mechanical Methods of Outpatient Ripening of the Cervix
Char: Participants:
185 women

Inclusion criteria: women aged between 39 and 41 weeks of gestational age who desire elective induction of labour based on reliable estimated gestational age (defined as ultrasonography performed before 14 weeks 0 days, or a certain last menstrual period consistent with ultrasonography performed before 21 weeks 0 days).

Exclusion criteria: women who have risk factors for placental insufficiency or intrapartum complications, such as intra-uterine growth restriction, hypertensive disease, insulin-requiring diabetes, multiple gestation, previous hysterotomy, cholestasis of pregnancy, placental abnormalities, maternal cardiac or pulmonary disease, known fetal anomaly, or fetal demise. Additionally, exclusion criteria include a Simplified Bishop score ≥6, cervical dilation ≥2 cm, inability to give informed consent, concerns regarding fetal well-being, conditions precluding vaginal birth, carrier status for group B streptococcus, and positive HIV, Hepatitis B, or Hepatitis C status. Women allergic to povidone-iodine, aquacryl hydrogel, or the latex-free Foley catheter will also be excluded.
Char: Interventions: Balloon catheters Vs Osmotic cervical dilators
Char: Outcomes: Pain, women's satisfaction, mode of delivery, shoulder dystocia, intra-amniotic infection, haemorrhage, APGAR score, Base excess >12, Umbilical cord gas pH <7, adverse neonatal outcomes, and serious maternal morbidity or mortality.

Char: Study name: Labor Induction With Double Balloon Device, Oral Misoprostol and Concomitant Use of Both
Char: Participants:
250 women

Inclusion criteria: a Bishop score of ≤4 indicating an unfavourable cervix, a medical or obstetrical indication for induction of labour, completion of 37 gestational weeks, vertex presentation of the fetus, singleton pregnancy, and intact membranes.

Exclusion criteria: previous cesarean delivery or uterine surgery such as myomectomy, non-cephalic presentation of the fetus, multiple pregnancies, pre-eclampsia with severe features, oligohydramnios (defined as maximal vertical pocket ≤2), estimated fetal weight below the 10th percentile, and any contraindication to vaginal delivery.
Char: Interventions: Oral misoprostol (25 or 50 µg) Vs Balloon catheters Vs Balloon catheters plus misoprostol
Char: Outcomes: Bishop score, time from induction to delivery, use of other ripening methods, rate of achieving active phase of labour, caesarean section, maternal morbidity, women's satisfaction, tachysystole, neonatal morbidity, oxytocin augmentation, use of emergent tocolysis, and doses of misoprostol.

Char: Study name: Labor Induction With Misoprostol Versus Oxytocin in Women With Premature Rupture of Membranes
Char: Participants:
200 women

Inclusion criteria: Women experiencing their first to fourth delivery with term prelabour rupture of membranes (37+0 to 42+0 weeks gestational age), singleton pregnancy, and vertex presentation are included in the study.

Exclusion criteria: multiple pregnancies, prior cesarean sections, chorioamnionitis upon admission, more than 2 symptomatic uterine contractions in 10 minutes, hypersensitivity to prostaglandins, and contraindications for vaginal delivery.
Char: Interventions: Oral misoprostol (25 or 50 µg) Vs Oxytocin (alone)
Char: Outcomes: Vaginal delivery, caesarean section, chorioamnionitis, uterine tachysystole, and neonatal morbidity.

Char: Study name: Management of Prelabor Rupture of the Membranes at Term
Char: Participants:
524 women

Inclusion criteria: primiparous women with singleton pregnancies admitted with prelabour rupture of membranes at a gestational age of 37 weeks and above, all presenting with a vertex presentation.

Exclusion criteria: women aged 18 and under, those with high-order gestation, contraindications for vaginal delivery, active labour, documented fetal anomalies, suspected intrauterine infection (temperature > 38 degrees, leucocytosis), non-reassuring fetal heart rate tracing, and positive group B streptococcus status.
Char: Interventions: Oxytocin (alone) Vs Expectant management
Char: Outcomes: Maternal infectious morbidity, length of latent and active phases of labour, haemorrhage, maternal death, ICU admission, stillbirth, neonatal infection, APGAR score, umbilical artery pH < 7.0, neonatal intensive care unit admission, RDS, and use of mechanical ventilation.

Char: Study name: Artificial Induction of Labour in Full-term Singleton Pregnancy : Comparative Randomized Trial of Two Strategies
Char: Participants:
450 women

Inclusion criteria: women with singleton pregnancies, cephalic fetal presentation, intact membranes between 37 and 42 weeks of amenorrhea, medical indication for labour induction as per the "Haute Autorité de Santé" (HAS) guidelines, an unfavourable cervix (Bishop scoring < 7), age over 18 years, affiliation with a healthcare system, and proficiency in the French language.

Exclusion criteria: history of previous caesarean section or uterine incision, placenta previa, unexplained metrorrhagia, lethal fetal abnormality, hyperreactivity to induction agents (dinoprostone or oxytocin) or latex, participation in another biomedical study, and individuals under legal guardianship or curatorship.
Char: Interventions: Controlled-release dinoprostone vaginal pessary Vs Balloon catheters
Char: Outcomes: Mode of delivey, time from induction to delivey, rate of peridural anaesthesia during labour, uterine hyperstimulation with and without changes of fetal heartbeats, uterine hypertonia, post-partum haemorrhage, uterine rupture, intra-uterine infections, post-partum infections, neonatal asphyxia, neonatal intensive care unit admission, neonatal infection, pain, and women's satisfaction.

Char: Study name: DOuble-BAlloon Versus PROstaglandin E2 for Cervical Ripening in Low Risk Pregnancies
Char: Participants:
540 women

Inclusion criteria: maternal age ≥ 18, singleton pregnancy with no recent reduction from a twin gestation after 14 weeks gestational age, randomization between 39+0 to 40+6 weeks of gestation, cephalic presentation, intact membranes, an unfavourable cervix (Bishop<6), and informed consent.

Exclusion criteria: maternal medical conditions posing risks to pregnancy outcomes (such as diabetes, hypertension, cardiac or renal issues, HIV, mental disorders), abnormal placenta conditions (including previa, accreta, or vasa previa), abnormal amniotic fluid volume (oligo- or polyhydramnios), abnormal fetal conditions (demise, anomalies, growth restriction, non-reassuring status), previous caesarean section, planned or contraindicated caesarean section, cervical interventions in current pregnancy, refusal of blood products, and participation in other studies affecting labour or perinatal outcomes.
Char: Interventions: Controlled-release dinoprostone vaginal pessary Vs Balloon catheters
Char: Outcomes: Mode of delivery, side effects, requring more than one induction agent, oxytocin augmentation, uterine hyperstimulation, time from induction to delivery, vaginal delivery within 24 hours, post-partum haemorrhage, uterine atony, hypertension complications, uterine dehiscence or rupture, maternal infection, hysterectomy, intensive care unit admission, matermal death, maternal and neonatal length of stay, psychometric aspects, APGAR score, neonatal intensive care unit admission, birth trauma, neonates with hypoglycemia, hypoxic ischemic encephalopathy or need for therapeutic hypothermia, meconium aspiration syndrome, neonates in need for respiratory supports, neonatal infection, and neonatal deaths.

Char: Study name: Foley Catheter Versus PGE2 for Labor Induction at Term: a Pilot Study
Char: Participants:
200 women

Inclusion criteria: women scheduled for labour induction, aged 18 or older, at least 37 weeks pregnant with a live singleton cephalic presentation, intact membranes, a cervical Bishop score below 6, and who provide informed consent.

Exclusion criteria: contraindications for vaginal delivery, prior cesarean section, known hypersensitivity to Foley catheter or prostaglandin E2, non-reassuring fetal status, and lethal fetal congenital anomalies.
Char: Interventions: Balloon catheters Vs Vaginal dinoprostone
Char: Outcomes: Perinatal complications, vaginal delivery, caesarean section, neonates need for respiratory support, perinatal deaths, neonatal intensive care unit admission, APGAR score < 7 at 1 and 5 minutes, maternal complications, postpartum hemorrhage, hysterectomy, intensive care unit admission, uterine rupture, and mater death, maternal satisfaction.
Char: Contact information: Zehong Zhou, Guangzhou Women and Children's Medical Center

Char: Study name: To Study the Efficacy and Safety of Misoprostol by Sublingual Routes for Induction of Labour
Char: Participants:
500 women

Inclusion criteria: women aged 18 years or older, primigravida, with singleton pregnancies at 41 weeks gestation or later, estimated fetal weight below 4000 grams, cephalic presentation, Bishop score less than 6 indicating an unfavourable cervix, and a reassuring fetal heart rate tracing.

Exclusion criteria: women under 18 years old, multiple pregnancies, gestation less than 41 weeks, fetal macrosomia (estimated fetal weight exceeding 4000 grams), cephalo-pelvic disproportion, malpresentation (breech, oblique, transverse), Bishop score exceeding 6 indicating a favourable cervix, presence of labour or uterine contractions, non-reassuring fetal heart rate tracing, allergy to misoprostol, previous caesarean delivery or other uterine surgery, previous uterine rupture, placenta previa, chorioamnionitis, prelabor rupture of membrane (PROM), antepartum haemorrhage (per vaginal bleeding), contraindication to vaginal birth, medical disorders in pregnancy, and active genital herpes infection, or invasive cervical carcinoma.
Char: Interventions: Sublingual or buccal misoprostol Vs Vaginal misoprostol
Char: Outcomes: Vaginal delivery within 24 hours, dosages of misoprostol, mode of delivery, time from induction to delivery.
Char: Contact information: Yeshey Dorjey, Ministry of Health, Bhutan, email: yesheydorjey@gmail.com

Char: Study name: Cook Balloon vs Dilapan-S for Outpatient Cervical Ripening
Char: Participants:
80 women

Inclusion criteria: women aged 18 to 50, at term (37 to 41 6/7 weeks gestational age), considered low risk without maternal or fetal co-morbidities, suitable for outpatient cervical ripening following the Brigham and Women's outpatient cervical ripening protocol, and with singleton pregnancy in cephalic presentation.

Exclusion criteria: women with prior cesarean section, any contraindication to outpatient cervical ripening as per the Brigham and Women's outpatient cervical ripening protocol, and non-English-speaking participants.
Char: Interventions: Osmotic cervical dilators Vs Balloon catheters
Char: Outcomes: Change in Bishop Score, maternal satisfaction, mode of delivery, time from induction to delvery, time from induction to vaginal delvery, maternal length of stay, Bishop score, maternal and neonatal morbidity, and regional analgesia
Char: Contact information: Sarah E Little, Brigham and Women's Hospital

Char: Study name: Induction of Labor in Pregnant Women With Prelabor Rupture of Membranes - Oxytocin or Misoprostol
Char: Participants:
200 women

Inclusion criteria: women with a gestational age between 36 and 42 weeks, experiencing prelabour rupture of membranes within the last 24 hours, and presenting with vertex presentation.

Exclusion criteria: a history of medical conditions such as hypertension, diabetes mellitus, systemic lupus erythematosus, and cardiac issues. Additionally, individuals with antepartum haemorrhage, chorioamnionitis lasting over 24 hours, multiple pregnancies, abnormal fetal heart rate patterns at admission, intrauterine growth restriction, fetal malpresentation, previous uterine scars, estimated fetal weight exceeding 4kg, those already in labour, or contraindications for prostaglandin/oxytocin use are excluded.
Char: Interventions: Vaginal misoprostol Vs Oxytocin
Char: Outcomes: Vaginal delivery, time from induction to delivery, APGAR score, neonatal intensive care unit admission, and maternal side effects.
Char: Contact information: Rania Hassan Mostafa, Ain Shams Maternity Hospital

Char: Study name: Dinoprostone Induction vs. Expectant Management After PROM at Term
Char: Participants:
70 women

Inclusion criteria: women aged 18 to 50 experiencing prelabour rupture of membranes within 4 to 12 hours. Additionally, participants must have parity ranging from 0 to 2, singleton pregnancies with a cephalic presentation, and fall within term gestational age (37 to 41 6/7 weeks). A Bishop score of 5 or less and a reassuring fetal status are also required for inclusion.

Exclusion criteria: women experiencing uterine contractions, signs of infection, non-reassuring fetal status, or meconium-stained amniotic fluid. Additionally, those with Group B Streptococcus colonization, fetal demise, major congenital anomalies, or intrauterine growth restriction (estimated fetal weight ≤ 3 percentile) are excluded. Moreover, individuals with contraindications for a vaginal birth or the use of prostaglandins for labour induction are also excluded.
Char: Interventions: Controlled-release dinoprostone vaginal pessary Vs Expectant managment
Char: Outcomes: Time from induction to delivery, time from PROM to delivery, mode of delivery, oxytocin augmentation, uterine hyperstimulation, chorioamnionitis, endometritis, postpartum maternal fever, use of antibiotics, neonatal intensive care unit admission, APGAR score, maternal length of stay, neonatal sepsis, and maternal satisfaction.
Char: Contact information: Polona Peclin, University Medical Centre Ljubljana, email: polona.peclin@kclj.si

Char: Study name: Balloon + Oxytocin Versus Oral Misoprostol to Induce Labor in Case of PROM (RUBAPRO2)
Char: Participants:
520 women

Inclusion criteria: women aged over 18, pregnant with a gestational age of ≥ 37 weeks, and having a singleton pregnancy with cephalic presentation. Additionally, nulliparous women with pre-labour rupture of membranes (PROM) beyond 12 hours, an unfavourable cervix (Bishop score < 6), and the ability to provide informed consent and comply with study requirements are included. Participants covered by the French Social Security welfare system are also eligible.

Exclusion criteria: women unable to comprehend French, those with contraindications for vaginal delivery, and instances of loss of meconium amniotic fluid. Additionally, exclusion factors include elevated temperature (>38.2°C), intrauterine infection, and fetal anomalies such as intrauterine growth restriction with Doppler anomalies or expected polymalformative syndrome. Moreover, contraindications involve a scarred womb, suspicion of genital herpes, and known HIV seropositivity, among others. These criteria also preclude participants with abnormal fetal heart rates, contraindications to misoprostol or balloon use, and contraindications to oxytocin, including dystocia and cardiovascular disorders. Lastly, refusal to participate and legal protection orders are considered exclusionary.
Char: Interventions: Balloon catheters plus oxytocin Vs Oral misoprostol
Char: Outcomes: Vaginal delivery within 24 hours, maternal satisfaction, time from induction to delivery, Bishop score, mode of delivery, post-partum hemorrhage, fever, uterine hyperstimulation, endometritis, duration of hospital stay, birth weight, Apgar score, pH umbilical artery, neonatal intensive care unit admission, and maternal and neonatal infection.

Char: Study name: Prostaglandins Versus Trans-cervical Balloon for Induction of Labor in Fetal Growth Restriction (PROBIN)
Char: Participants:
774 women

Inclusion criteria: women aged over 18 years with singleton gestation and cephalic presentation. Gestational age at randomization ranges between 34 weeks and 41 weeks. Fetal growth restriction (FGR), as defined by the trial DIGITAT, includes an abdominal circumference or estimated fetal weight below the 10th percentile. This criterion applies regardless of Doppler index status. Additionally, candidates must have a plan for induction of labour, regardless of indication. A Bishop Score below 6, affiliation with a health security system, and signed informed consent are also required.

Exclusion criteria: contraindications to induction of labour and a history of previous cesarean delivery or myomectomy. Contraindications to misoprostol or trans-cervical balloon insertion, known HIV positivity, major fetal or chromosomal anomalies, fetal demise, and legal protection status also lead to exclusion. Additionally, poor understanding of the French language is grounds for exclusion.
Char: Interventions: Balloon catheters Vs Vaginal misoprostol
Char: Outcomes: Caesarean section, time from induction to delivery, oxytocin augmentation, postpartum haemorrhage, blood loss, intra-uterine infectious, maternal thromboembolism, maternal satisfaction, duration of hospitalisation, umbilical artery lactic acid, APGAR score, neonatal hypoglycemia, neonatal intensive care unit admission, neonatal death, fetal distress, neonatal ventilation, and adverse neonatal outcomes.

Char: Study name: Oral and Vaginal Misoprostol for Induction of Labor in Nulliparous Pregnant Women
Char: Participants:
80 women

Inclusion criteria: women aged between 18 and 40, nulliparity, indicating women who have never carried a pregnancy beyond 20 weeks, and single living pregnancy. Gestational age must be at or beyond completed 41 weeks, confirmed by reliable dating methods. A cephalic presentation and a Bishop score of 6 or less are required. Additionally, a reactive fetal non-stress test (NST) is necessary for inclusion.

Exclusion criteria: any maternal chronic diseases or pregnancy-induced medical disorders, fetal anomalies, fetal macrosomia (>4 Kg), intrauterine growth restriction (IUGR) (estimated fetal weight below the 10th percentile for gestational age), rupture of membranes or oligohydramnios (amniotic fluid index < the fifth percentile), previous uterine scar, regular uterine contractions, and any contraindication to vaginal delivery, such as placenta previa (complete or partial covering of the internal os of the cervix with the placenta).
Char: Interventions: Vaginal misoprostol Vs Oral misoprostol
Char: Outcomes: Onset of active stage of labour, caesarean section, doses of misoprostol given, oxytocin augmentation, and complications.

Char: Study name: A Randomized Trial Comparing Foley Catheter, Oxytocin and combination Foley catheter-Oxytocin for Induction of Labour with Unfavourable Cervix
Char: Participants:
108 women

Inclusion criteria: singleton pregnancies at 28 weeks or more, requiring induction of labour due to medical indications and with an unfavourable cervix will be included if there are no contraindications for vaginal delivery.

Exclusion criteria: maternal or fetal contraindication for induction of labour
Char: Interventions: Oxytocin (alone) Vs Balloon catheters Vs Balloon catheters plus oxytocin
Char: Outcomes: Bishop score, time from induction to cervical ripening, time from induction to delivery, mode of delivery, and adverse maternal and neonatal outcomes.

Char: Study name: Efficacy of vaginal misoprostol and cervical foley catheter versus vaginal misoprostol alone on term pregnancy labour induction in enugu: a randomized controlled trial
Char: Participants:
132 women

Inclusion criteria: woman scheduled for labour induction at term (37 completed weeks to 41 weeks + 6 days gestation) with an unfavourable cervix (Bishop score < 6), who consents and has a live singleton fetus in a longitudinal lie with cephalic presentation and reactive non-stress test, will be included.

Exclusion criteria: women at term who do not provide consent, have contraindications to vaginal delivery, are carrying multiple fetuses, have experienced intrauterine fetal death, have an anomalous fetus, show nonreactive stress test results, have a history of prior uterine rupture or surgery, experience regular uterine contractions, exhibit vaginal bleeding, or have experienced premature rupture of membranes will be excluded.
Char: Interventions: Vaginal misoprostol Vs Balloon catheters plus misoprostol
Char: Outcomes: Time from induction to vaginal delivery, vaginal delivery, oxytocin augmentation, APGAR score, neonatal intensive care unit admission, uterine hyperstimulation, uterine rupture, fetal heart rate abnormalities, and caesarean section.

Char: Study name: A Randomized Controlled Trial on Expectant versus Active Management with Sublingual Prostaglandin E-1 Analogue for Term Premature Rupture of the Fetal Membranes
Char: Participants:
86 women

Inclusion criteria: women with gestational ages between 37 weeks and 41 weeks plus 2 days, singleton pregnancies, maternal ages between 20 and 34 years, confirmation of an adequate pelvis, vertex fetal presentation, cervical dilatation less than 4cm, and confirmation of a live fetus with normal cardiotocography (CTG) readings and ultrasound findings.

Exclusion criteria: women aged below 20 or above 34 years, gestational ages outside the range of 37 weeks to 41 weeks plus 2 days, multiple pregnancies, chorioamnionitis, medical disorders in pregnancy, obstetric complications, grand multiparity, previous caesarean delivery, meconium-stained liquor, cephalopelvic disproportion, malpresentation, intrauterine fetal death, prolonged premature rupture of membranes (PROM), cervical dilatation up to 4cm, pregnancies resulting from in vitro fertilization, multiple vaginal examinations prior to presentation, and cervical incompetence.
Char: Interventions: Sublingual misoprostol Vs Expectant management
Char: Outcomes: Mode of delivery, time from induction to delivery, postpartum haemorrhage, APGAR score, and neonatal intensive care unit admission.

Char: Study name: Labor induction with synthetic prostaglandins in obese woman
Char: Participants:
Inclusion criteria: nulliparous or multiparous pregnant obese women at 37 weeks of gestational age with a Bishop score less than or equal to 6.

Exclusion criteria: multiple pregnancies, anomalous fetal presentations, unexplained vaginal bleeding, and abnormal placentation including placenta previa, vasa previa, or placenta accreta. Additionally, previous uterine scarring, active liver, kidney, lung, or heart disease, systemic or local infectious diseases, and allergy to any prostaglandins are grounds for exclusion.
Char: Interventions: Vaginal misoprostol Vs Controlled-release dinoprostone vaginal pessary
Char: Outcomes: Success of cervical ripening, time from induction to cervical ripening, oxytocin augmentation, tachysystole, fetal distress, dystocia, mode of delivery, and maternal adverse outcomes.

Char: Study name: Comparison of different approaches to labour induction among multi parous women at term
Char: Participants:
Inclusion criteria: multiparous women undergoing induction of labour at the study setting, with gestation exceeding 40+4 weeks. Additionally, eligibility requires a singleton pregnancy with cephalic presentation and unruptured membranes. Furthermore, candidates must have a Modified Bishop Score (MBS) of less than 8.

Exclusion criteria: primiparity and malpresentation with an unstable lie. Additionally, exclusion criteria include a Modified Bishop Score (MBS) of 8 or above, any contraindication to vaginal birth due to previous uterine surgery (including caesarean section, placenta previa, and other placental anomalies), age less than 18 years, lethal fetal congenital anomaly, and known allergy to any of the interventional products.
Char: Interventions: Vaginal dinoprostone Vs Balloon catheters Vs Membrance sweeping Vs Expectant management
Char: Outcomes: Time from induction to delivery, failed induction, oxytocin augmentation, uterine hyperstimulation, mode of delivery, blood loss, maternal pyrexia, perineal lacerations, APGAR score, and neonatal intensive care unit admission.

Char: Study name: Effectiveness and safety of oral misoprostol Vs intravaginal PGE2 (Dinoprostone) for pre-induction cervical ripening in women with uncomplicated, singleton, post dated pregnancies: a randomized controlled study
Char: Participants:
250 women

Inclusion criteria: nulliparous pregnant women with a singleton pregnancy at 40 weeks and 5 days of gestation, featuring a fetus in cephalic presentation with intact membranes and a modified Bishop score (MBS) of < 5. Additionally, participants must not have any contraindications for vaginal delivery.

Exclusion criteria: women with a history of past caesarian delivery or myomectomy, as well as those with hypersensitivity to misoprostol. Additionally, exclusion extends to cases of pregnancy-induced hypertension, gestational diabetes mellitus, and multiple pregnancies.
Char: Interventions: Oral misoprostol Vs Vaginal dinoprostone
Char: Outcomes: Spontaneous onset of labour, time from induction to delivery, caesarean section, uterine hyperstimulation, post partum haemorrhage, uterine rupture, meconium stained liquor, APGAR score, and neonatal intensive care unit admission.
